[b]Pan-Shamatism[/b]

[i]1976, West and East Shamat[/i]

[i](based upon the irl ideology of Pan-Eurasianism, but different ;)[/i]

[b]----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------[/b]

As many of yall know, Shamat is the combined continents of East, and West Shamat.

Although differences are present, people from Shamat always have had a feeling of a bond with each other, especially compared to their connections with other continents. Neo-Colonialism is still present at all current times, and people usually don't like those nations being present on their continents, some exceptions are very much present, but there will always be a feeling of external influences.

50 years ago, something ignited, something started, in a lot of forms and identities, but it was still unknown, [i]sadly[/i]. Many forms and versions existed, you can call them what you want; left, right, progressive, conservative, extreme, centrist and beyond. Even people from Shamat, who were outside Shamat, felt a connection to this idea, to this concept.

It grew and it grew, at some point every single person in a city would know about it. The Idea of Shamatism and/or Pan-Shamatism. BUT, the problem was, no one was truly expressing it yet, and no one truly saw it as something doable. Until one certain day in the Sikirskian province of Zirsk, to be precise, in the now-very-important city of [b]Kerlgrad:[/b]

[b]-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[/b]

[b]A Congress![/b]

Good Evening gentlemen and gentlewomen of Shamat! I, Volodymyr Uladzimir, welcome you to the first Pan-Shamatist Congress of [i]1984[/i]

Our idea has grown and expanded a lot, this congress was something we have been waiting for too long already! Shamat and its people have been waiting too long for this...

I have recently founded the Sikirskian Pan-Shamatist Salvation Party, and as planned it has grown to a national scale. I see many of you here, from the Far East, to the Far West.

We may not be [b]there[/b] yet, but do not falter. It will only get better from now on.

[i][b] "What is a United Shamat?"[/b][/i]

[i]--The room erupts into clapping and cheering.--[/i]

[b]-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[/b]

[b]Define; Modern Day Chaos[/b]

Welcome to the evening broadcast, citizens of the Federatsiya. As lately revealed, the [b]CTO+[/b] Coalition government has fallen. Marshal-Prezident Mitarski has announced that he is aware of the current situation. The situations outcome is unknown. Mass protests have spiraled out of control, major cities with this situation include; Grand Yugorsk, New & Old Liberatska City, [b]Kerlgrad[/b], and Likastad. Besides that, we have just received new estimate poll results, SPSSP has had a once again major increase in popularity, 49,7%, CTO, 29,2%, RCS: 12,9%, NPA: 7,0%, RAU: 0,9%. We keep you updated whenever possible, [i]Drobyden, good night.[/i]

[i]What could ever go wrong? :)[/i]

[/spoiler]

[spoiler=Abdullah al-Barazakhs Inaugural Speech as First Secretary General of the EOIC]

Makkah (current HQ of the EOIC, as long as thats ok with whatever country in RP owns it), 26 October 2026 Delegates and observers from the participating states of the EOIC convened in the courtyard of the Quba Mosque [the first mosque built after the conquest of Makkah by Islamic forces in 630] along with a throng of guests and interested residents from the city to hear the new Secretary General, Abdullah al-Barazakh, give a speech and outline his priorities for the organization. Even some curious camels were milling about, clearly not bothered by the people trying to get them to leave. 

Bismillah ir Rahman ir Raheem, walhamdulillah wastainu wasalaam alaa sayyidina Muhammad, wa alaa alihi wa sahbihi wa sallim. As salaamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh. Amma bad.

I begin in the name of Allah Almighty, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful, and all praise is due to Allah and I seek refuge in Him. May he send His blessings and peace upon our worldly master Muhammad (salallahu alayhi wa sallim) and his family, companions, and all who follow his Sunnah. I also extend my peace and blessings to all of you here today. To begin:

Thank you for having trust and faith in me to lead this organization, one that reflects the highest aim of organizations in the dunya: building the unity and strength of the Ummah to please Allah, obey His laws in everything we do, and follow the way of His Final Messenger and Prophet, Muhammad (salallahu alayhi wa sallim). 

When I was initially called upon by the Sultan of Baladullah himself to be my countrys candidate for Secretary General, I declined out of fear of being held accountable before Allah Almighty, and having no love for worldly authority. But after we talked for some time over a couple of days, I realized that this trust was something Allah had extended to me. While I am in no way even similar to Abu Bakr (may Allah be please with him), I did think of how he overcame his hesitation and dislike of authority to accept the nomination as the first Khalif (worldly successor) of the Prophet (salallahu alayhi wa sallim), and Alhamdullilah that he did. I am pleased that our leaders still uphold the Prophetic Sunnah of not giving leadership to those who seek it out, but on the basis of nomination, and in shaa Allah this system remains until the day of judgment. 

I ask you all to never be afraid to correct me if I am wrong, let me know if I have transgressed any boundaries, and hold me to account in this life lest my accountability only arrives from Allah Almighty on the Day of Resurrection. I ask Allah Almighty to help me to carry out my responsibility and duties to the fullest degree, in conformity with the Quran, the Sunnah, and the methodology of Ahl as-Sunnah wal Jamaa (the united community of Muslims). 

As for priorities for the organization, I believe first and foremost we must seek to facilitate peace and reconciliation between the parties involved in the conflict in Valddera, as long as they are all willing and able to accept mediation and a peace settlement, in shaa Allah. Secondly, establishing a General Fund based on voluntary contributions from all member states to fund Islamic education, charities, social services, and a zakat system for the EOIC. I have been talking with the Ministry of Zakat in Baladullah, and he has said that the government is willing to give 2.5% of its yearly budget towards this fund, in shaa Allah. Third would be a free and fair trade agreement between all participant nations, with an emphasis on countries trading for the benefit of all involved, and the possible establishment of a no-interest loan system for investment and development, which could be paid back in either currency or resources. 

In shaa Allah this is the beginning of a successful pan-Islamic project that will not only materially and spiritually uplift the Ummah, but bring benefit to all humanity as well. Thank you.
[/spoiler]

[spoiler=The Non-Aligned Bloc (NAB)][b]Jincheon Special Metropolitan City, Minhokae[/b]

It was the 24th of October and Jincheon was in its usual routine. People rushing to work, school buses carrying children to school, pedestrians crossing the street, subways in full swing; the usual. Today happened to be different. There was the Prime Minister, waiting to take the subway. Ko Jong-hyuk, an odd man at times, decided to take the subway simply because "he felt like it." There was something about the subway that he loved, whether it was seeing the bustling people or simply the trains in action, he felt alive when he didn't have to show up to work in the usual vehicle convoy that he didn't care much for. He approached an elderly woman and asked if he could sit next to her. After receiving permission, the Prime Minister began his usual conversation starter. "How are you doing today, ma'am?" "I'm doing alright, young man. Praise the Lord. Might I ask why you asked me how I am doing? One doesn't see many people interested about others nowadays." It was clear that the elderly woman didn't care about what role the person she was speaking to had. She probably didnt even know his job. She just cared about decent conversation. "I believe our society needs to  wake up, ma'am. We need to be more considerate of our elders and contribute to this society more." "You know, that's the first time I've heard that in many years. Where are you from, boy?" Gangwon Province, maam. Well youre a fine young man. Say, would you give me some advice on a birthday gift for my grandson? Here he is. She showed him a picture of the little boy on her phone, and she smiled and happily said Isnt he just the cutest thing? Indeed maam. What about a toolbox? My son loves those. May I see a picture of him? Yes maam, here he is. You youth know how to use technology so quickly these days! She said as he unlocked his phone and found a picture of his son. Oh, look at him. Hes beautiful! Thank you maam. Well, its been a pleasure talking to you. Wait. Can you help me up, boy? Its my stop too. Oh, forgive me maam. He helped her up, and the speaker came on. NATIONAL ASSEMBLY STATION. Have a blessed day, maam. he said.You too. she responded. People looked at him as he walked by, realizing that it was the Prime Minister, and soon enough, he began to accumulate a crowd. Hello everyone. Fine day isnt it? He said, as he walked by hurriedly. He knew it took him 4 minutes to get to the National Assembly Parliament Building, and he knew that if he walked fast enough, he would make it to his meeting right on time. It was only about 200 meters from the subway station, so he wasnt worried. His phone rang and he picked up. Hello? Sir, its me Chang-ho. The meeting starts in 3 minutes. Tell them Ill be there in 2. Yes sir, thank you. He hung up. Chang-ho was his personal assistant and he could tell he cared. He would feel bad about letting him down, so he sped up. The elevator doors opened right away when he pressed the button, and he walked in. There was 1 minute until his meeting started. The elevator dinged, and he walked out and into the conference room. Good morning Chang-ho, hello all. His cabinet pulled out their papers from their briefcases, pulled their computers out, and pulled out their pens. We have a very busy day today, so lets get going. First up, our Non-Aligned Bloc outline.

[b]The Non-Aligned Bloc[/b]

Alright everyone. Get comfortable, this is going to be a more important meeting. The Prime Minister picked up a pointer stick and smacked the whiteboard. As you all know, weve been laying out the framework for a deal that we think should be made involving us countries who refuse to get involved in the conflicts between EDU and THEP. Before we make this public and available to other countries, we should work on these topics first:
 - The sovereignty, Independence, and territorial integrity of all members states must be respected
 - Peaceful coexistence among member nations is a priority, and every nation must commit to rejecting
   alignment with any military or ideological blocs
 - Economic cooperation can be fostered in any major and legal area
 - The Non-Aligned Bloc will be kept open for any sovereign state that commits to the principles of neutrality, nonaggression, and mutual respect
 - Should a military conflict occur between nations in the NAB, they are expected to resolve it themselves quickly and efficiently, with members choosing to apply sanctions or call for an end to the conflict in a stern way
 - The annual summit of heads of state to set strategic direction will be known as the Council of Sovereigns
 -  The permanent administrative body which coordinates initiatives and communication will be known as the Equilibrium Secretariat
 - Every two years, a member state assumes leadership which can be used to host summits and represent the NAB Internationally
 - Members will not participate in foreign military alliances or host foreign military bases
 - The Non-Aligned Bloc will establish the Equilibrium Development Bank to fund infrastructure, education, and innovation
 - Fair trade agreements and technology will be promoted and shared among members
 - Joint research initiatives will be conducted in energy, agriculture, digital sovereignty, and more
 - Creation of the NAB fellowship program for students, artists, researches, and many more fields
 - Protection of linguistic and cultural diversity as the base for national identity
 - NAB will maintain diplomatic relations with nations of their choosing
 - NAB may issue joint statements on crises around the world, emphasizing neutrality
 - Regardless of what the NAB votes for as a whole, any nation has the right to emphasize its own opinion on matters
 - Amendments will require a two-thirds majority vote in the Council of Sovereigns
 - Members of the NAB will be able to withdraw whenever they see fit
 - The selling of natural resources between members is encouraged and viewed as economic cooperation
Is everyone in agreement? His cabinet discussed, and finally one member spoke up. Sir, we recommend that you change Economic cooperation can be fostered in any major and legal area to  Economic cooperation can be fostered in any major and legal area with permission from the authorities of that area. Alright, I find that reasonable. All in agreement say aye. AYE they responded. All opposed? No answer. Alright, Ill take it up with the King. That was rather productive, and, thank you all for your cooperation. The Prime Minister bowed, turned around, briefcase in hand, and walked out the door.

[b]Meeting with His Majesty, the King[/b]

Using the back entrance of the Parliament Building, he got in his vehicle and gave permission for the driver to start the drive. To get to Deoksugung Palace where the King lived, it took about 40 minutes. So he sat back, pulled out his computer, and started to respond to lengthy emails, requests, view national security briefings, etc. The normal jobs of a Prime Minister. The monarchs of Minhokae had a tradition of not staying in the political area of the capital, preferring to live a more private life aside from politics. Despite monarchs holding significant political power, they have all been gentlemen and only used their power efficiently. It cannot be said that monarchs did not intervene politically, though. Whenever the rare times came up when parliamentarians would become uncivil and sometimes even have physical altercation, the King would pay a surprise visit to the National Assembly and harshly rebuke them. He wouldnt leave until they apologized to one another, and sorted out their problems. They would feel ashamed, while the King would enjoy himself. He offered advice to his ministers very often, and would keep them in check. Of course, he couldnt propose laws, but could veto them and act in his own right only in times of national emergency. The population itself enjoyed many laughs seeing parliamentarians being rebuked by the King, and it was a primary component of the Kings popularity. He kept up with the times, and made regular visits all around Minhokae, including rural, urban, and suburban areas alike, though he liked rural areas the most. Many times he would crack a joke or two, and but is also very smart. Educated at the University of Jincheon with a major in political science and a minor in geography, its safe to say that politicians did not outmaneuver him. Though he granted substantial rights to Parliament, his ministers, and the Prime Minister himself, he held the ultimate political authority in the country, which is largely based on tradition and respect for the monarch. Minhoake is a very traditional country. King Peter Chung Soon-taick (baptismal name Peter), of the Chung Dynasty did not care for politics much, but acted in the interest of his country. He was a patriot, there was no denying that. Whenever a political stance of Minhokae was to be advocated abroad, he sent ambassadors, but when there wasnt, he would go himself. The King never got into any political debates, but it was clear where he stood in many many aspects. As such, politicians generally avoided those questions around him, unless the King felt that they were trying to seek his approval in something controversial that he would not take part in. Knowing this, the Prime Minister held high respect for the King, and had careful and calculated conversations with him. Right here please, thank you. He got out of the car and began to walk up the stairs towards the Kings Audience Room, where the monarch had weekly consultations with the Prime Minister. Inside, the King fixed his watch on his wrist, adjusted his shirt collar, fixed the cuffs on his wrists, and stood up straight.  A man walked in and bowed. The Prime Minister is has arrived, sir the man was Do-yun Park, his aide-de-camp and personal secretary. Thank you, Do-yun. Send him in. Do-yun bowed and opened the doors.
